essence: A city that can only be told through images that mean their opposite: its filigree, peacocks and lantern-lit canoes stand for soot, grinding labour and sarcasm, while a city really made of those lovely things would be a black hole; falsehood lives in things, not in words.
textDetails: Marco tells Kublai that a city must never be confused with the words that describe it, and yet there is a connection between the two.
Olivia is rich in products and profits; its prosperity can only be conveyed by speaking of filigree palaces with fringed cushions on the seats by the mullioned windows.
Beyond the screen of a patio, spinning jets water a lawn where a white peacock spreads its tail.

From these words one grasps at once that Olivia is wrapped in a cloud of soot and grease that clings to the houses, and that in its brawling streets manoeuvring trailers crush pedestrians against the walls.
The inhabitants' industry is told through saddlers' shops smelling of leather, women chattering as they weave raffia rugs, and hanging canals whose cascades drive the paddles of mills.
The image these words evoke is the mandrel set against the teeth of the lathe, one action repeated by thousands of hands thousands of times at the pace fixed for each shift.
Olivia's leaning toward a free life and refined civilization is told through ladies gliding at night in illuminated canoes between the banks of a green estuary.

That image only recalls the outskirts where men and women 'land' every evening like lines of sleepwalkers, and where someone always bursts out laughing in the dark, setting loose a flow of jokes and sarcasm.
To speak of Olivia, no other words could be used.
If there really were an Olivia of mullioned windows and peacocks, of saddlers, rug-weavers, canoes and estuaries, it would be a wretched, black, fly-ridden hole.
To describe that city one would have to fall back on metaphors of soot, creaking wheels, repeated actions and sarcasm.
The closing idea: the lie is never in the words, it is in the things.
Not in the text: layout, scale or colours beyond the white peacock, the green estuary and the black soot; whether the evening crowds arrive by boat is uncertain ('land' may simply mean arrive).
visualConcept: Olivia is built as one set of forms with two complete readings, and the default reading is Marco's description: an exquisite evening city of ivory and gold filigree palaces whose walls are lace-like pierced screens and whose mullioned windows hold fringed cushions; a patio behind a carved screen where four spinning jets water a jewel-green lawn and a white peacock opens and closes its luminous fan; two hanging canals carried on slender arches across the city, their cascades turning mill paddles; saddlers' shops under leather-brown awnings and a courtyard of women at raffia looms; and a green estuary winding through the island, down which a procession of lantern-lit canoes glides in the dark. Every element is designed in shape-rhyme with what it signifies, so the second reading can grow out of it without changing the composition: the peacock's fan is the exact silhouette of a fan of black smoke from a stack, the whirling jets are lathe spindles, the mill paddles are flywheels, the looms are rows of identical workbenches, the canoe procession is a file of tired workers with dim lamps. The connection is already hinted in the default state: the low sun behind the city throws long shadows toward the viewer, and those shadows, cast by hidden shadow-only geometry (colorWrite off, castShadow on), are the silhouettes of smokestacks, sawtooth factory roofs and trailers, while the golden motes floating in the air are in fact soot. The base is a low dark island resting on still black water that merges with smog at the horizon, split by the green estuary running from the front edge into the mist behind. Nothing in the description is ever false; the toggle simply lets the things catch up with the words.
layout: Convention: +X east, -Z north. Island radius about 21, top at y=0, dark loam with pale paving inside the city, resting on still black water. Green estuary: a channel 5 wide at the south-west edge narrowing to 2 at the north-east, meandering through the centre, water at y=-0.3, quays on both banks. Filigree palaces: 12 along both banks, footprints 3 x 3 to 4 x 5, heights 3 to 6, walls of instanced pierced-lattice panels with arched mullioned windows and fringed cushions on the sills, domed or pavilion roofs. Patio: east bank near the centre, a screened court 5 x 5 with a 4 x 4 lawn, 4 rotating jets and the white peacock, slightly oversized as in a miniature (body 0.4 tall, tail fan radius 1.1). Hanging canals: two aqueducts on slender arches at y=5 and y=6.5, crossing the estuary at about 60 degrees to each other, each with 3 cascades falling onto paddle wheels (radius 0.8) in small mill houses. Saddlers' street: 8 small shops along the west bank; rug court: 6 seated women at raffia looms with bright rugs. Canoes: 9 (0.8 long), each with a hanging lantern and a seated lady, gliding in file along a looped path on the estuary. Outskirts: a ring of low row-houses at radius 15 to 20 and a landing quay at the estuary mouth. Things-state counterparts share the same footprints: palaces become soot-black tenements and sawtooth-roofed factory halls; the patio becomes a chimney yard with 3 stacks 7 to 9 tall; the jets become rows of lathes (40 benches, one figure each repeating a single stroke); the paddles become flywheels with belts; the canoes become 3 low barges unloading files of about 60 trudging figures with dim lamps toward the outskirts; 6 to 8 boxy trailers shunt through the streets.
signatureMotion: 1) In the words: the peacock opens and folds its tail every 15 s, the lawn jets whirl, cascades spill from the hanging canals and turn the paddle wheels, the lantern canoes glide in slow procession with trembling reflections on the green water. 2) The same rhythms in the things: the identical rotation now drives lathe spindles and flywheels at a hard mechanical tempo, rows of tiny hands repeat one stroke in unison to a shift bell, trailers shunt and pin figures against walls, black flakes fall where golden motes floated. 3) The laugh: in the outskirts, one figure in the file of sleepwalkers bursts out laughing, a small bright flare that ripples down the line as a chain of flickers, jokes and sarcasm spreading through the dark.
interactionDescription: Morphs each image of the description into the thing it signifies while keeping its outline: filigree walls silt up with soot and grease, the white peacock's fan becomes a plume of black smoke fanning from a stack, the whirling jets become lathe spindles in endless rows, the mill paddles become flywheels and belts, the lantern canoes become barges unloading files of sleepwalking workers, and the light turns furnace-orange under brown smog. The shadows swap roles as well: the grimy city now casts shadows in the shape of lace, because its only true description is the filigree. Toggle back and the description returns, intact and faithful.
mood: Evening turning to night. In the words: a warm, gilded dusk with lanterns, a jade glow rising off the estuary and the air sparkling with golden motes. In the things: the same hour seen through brown smog, furnace-orange light from below, sodium haze, blackened silhouettes and falling soot. Both states share the same low sun direction and composition so the morph reads as one place seen two ways.
caption: Olivia is rich, and the only way to say so is with filigree palaces, fringed cushions at mullioned windows, a white peacock opening its tail on a lawn kept wet by whirling jets. Hear those words rightly and you see soot and grease, trailers pinning people to walls, one lathe stroke repeated through every shift, files of sleepwalkers arriving at nightfall, a laugh cracking the dark. The words are faithful; if anything lies, it is the things.
motto: Speak of peacocks, and the wise will see the soot.
camera: From the estuary mouth at the south-west, distance about 32 units, elevation about 26 degrees, target (0, 2.5, 0): the green estuary and its canoe procession lead from the foreground into the city, the peacock patio sits just right of centre, the hanging canals cross the middle distance at mid-height, and the long shadows fall toward the camera so their hidden factory silhouettes read clearly on the ground.
